free_text_notes: 65F with known HFrEF (EF 30%) presents with 3 days of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. She has been non-adherent with her medications due to cost. On exam: BP 140/85, HR 95, RR 24, SpO2 88% on room air. JVP elevated to the jaw. Bilateral crackles. 2+ pitting edema to mid-thigh bilaterally.
ECHO: EF 25%, severely reduced. Moderate MR. No tamponade.
TREATMENT: IV furosemide 80 mg BID, supplemental O2, restart carvedilol and lisinopril at low doses, captopril challenge passed, transition to oral diuretics.
DISCHARGE: 4 days, weight down 6 kg, symptoms resolved. Discharge meds: furosemide 80 mg BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily. Close follow-up in 1 week.

original_qa.q: What brings you to the hospital?
original_qa.a: I've been getting more and more short of breath over the last few days. Even just walking to the bathroom makes me winded.

original_qa.q: Have you been taking your medications?
original_qa.a: Honestly, no. They're expensive and I ran out about a week ago. I should have called the office but I didn't.

original_qa.q: Are you able to lie flat to sleep?
original_qa.a: No, I have to sleep sitting up now. If I lie down I feel like I'm drowning.
Yes, my legs have gotten really swollen. My shoes don't fit anymore.

original_qa.q: What medications were you on before?
original_qa.a: Carvedilol, lisinopril, and a water pill called furosemide. And spironolactone.

original_qa.q: What did the doctors do for you?
original_qa.a: They gave me a strong water pill through my IV. I peed out a lot of fluid — I lost 6 kilograms. And they restarted my heart medications.
